title: Finite affine-cover alternating totalization of a quasi-coherent resolution
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $r\geq0$, and $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X_{\mathrm{open}}$ a family with $\bigcup_i U_i=X$. Suppose every intersection indexed by a nonempty tuple, allowing repetitions and empty opens, is affine. Let $F,J$ be unbounded cochain complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], every term of $F$ quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and $J$ K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For every quasi-isomorphism $i:F\to J$, the morphism $T_U(i):T_U(F)\to T_U(J)$ of the actual alternating total functor [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex] is a quasi-isomorphism. This assertion is about a specified cochain map, without localization or comparison-map data.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 08C2, affine-basis case using Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01XB; parent proof Steps 2--3

proof.text: Restrict i to every nonempty intersection. Restriction is exact and preserves K-injectivity. The affine quasi-coherent derived equivalence identifies ordinary sections of the termwise quasi-coherent complex with derived sections, compatibly with the ordinary-to-derived unit; the unbounded acyclic comparison removes the negative tail. The K-injective computation of derived sections then identifies the section map of i with this unit and proves it is a quasi-isomorphism. Quasi-coherent kernels and cokernels ensure that cohomology and good truncations remain quasi-coherent.

The products over increasing tuples in each Cech degree are finite. Kernels and images commute with these finite products of modules, so every column map is a quasi-isomorphism. The actual integer double complexes have zero columns outside 0 through r-1: negative columns are extended by zero and no strictly increasing (p+1)-tuple exists when p is at least r. Apply the existing upstream finite-column total comparison theorem with bounds 0 and r-1. Its finite induction on the stupid column filtration proves that T_U(i) is a quasi-isomorphism directly, without spectral sequences or page induction. When r=0 both totals vanish and the theorem also allows the empty interval.
